question: A seaside hotel has 165 rooms in its main building and 50 rooms in an annex. During a busy week, every room used 7 fresh towels each day for 7 days, and all the used towels were sent to the laundry, where a dozen staff work. The hotel has 6 floors. By the end of the week the laundry had returned 7647 towels clean. How many towels were still at the laundry?

Farmer Ana keeps 225 hens, and each hen laid 8 eggs this week. She packed the eggs 3 to a small box, and then bundled the boxes 3 to a crate. She sold every crate for 5 dollars at the market half a mile down the road. Out of that money she paid 416 dollars for feed, and then earned 25 dollars selling a bale of straw. Her neighbour Ben made less from his eggs this week than Ana. How many dollars does Ana have from this week's sales after paying for the feed?

Yusuf's travel purse held 170 pounds when he left home. His father gave him 49 pounds at the station, and the train ticket cost 114 pounds from the purse. At the border he changed every pound in the purse into lira at 5 lira per pound, in a queue that took an hour and a half, ninety minutes. His aunt then handed him 74 lira, and the hotel took 231 lira from the purse. His sister Zara, travelling with him, had fewer lira in her purse. How many lira were in Yusuf's purse after paying the hotel?

In the morning a tailor named Sofia cut 100 strips of silk from each of 3 bolts. She then found 9 spare strips in a drawer and 19 more in a bag from the previous week, and added them to the pile. In the afternoon she cut every strip into 8 equal squares for a patchwork quilt. In the evening she stitched 9 beads onto every square. Her apprentice Tomas stitched far fewer beads that day than Sofia. How many beads did Sofia stitch?

In the morning Priya's camera held 151 photos from her trip, and she deleted 23 blurry ones. In the afternoon she ordered 4 prints of every photo left on the camera and picked them all up from the shop. Her grandmother then gave her 80 old prints to add to the same album. In the evening Priya handed out 451 prints to relatives at a family dinner. How many prints did Priya have left?

Nora had 12 sheets of coloured paper. She used 10 of them for a school poster and gave 1 sheet to her brother. She cut every sheet she had left into 9 strips. She used 7 of the strips to make a paper chain. Then she cut each remaining strip into 5 small squares for confetti, and 1 square blew out of the window. How many squares of confetti does Nora have?

In the morning Farah won 216 tickets at the fair's ring toss and 80 more at the hoop game, keeping them all in one pouch. At the prize booth in the afternoon she exchanged every ticket for 5 tokens each. She then found 55 tokens under a bench and added them to the pouch. In the evening the booth switched to a special rate: she swapped every token for 2 stamps each, and every stamp was worth 8 points on the fair's leaderboard. How many points did Farah have on the leaderboard?

Greg had 119 sheets of stickers and was given 4 more sheets by his teacher. Every sheet carries 8 stickers, and he peeled them all off into one big pile. He then bundled the pile into packs of 6 stickers each, a job that took him two hours, one hundred and twenty minutes. Finally he gave half of the packs to his sister. How many packs of stickers does Greg have left?

In the morning the caterers set out 163 chairs in each of the 2 halls of the conference centre. In the afternoon 12 extra chairs were brought from the storeroom and 22 more were borrowed from the cafe. The stage at the front is 10 metres wide. In the evening a late delivery added 3 chairs, and the hotel next door lent 15 more. How many chairs were set out by the end of the evening?

In the morning a parcel depot loaded 106 crates onto each of its 8 trucks. In the afternoon the crates were opened at the sorting hall: every crate held 9 boxes, and every box held 9 parcels. The depot is 30 kilometres from the airport. In the evening 25 late parcels arrived by van and 13 more were handed in at the counter, all joining the day's sort. How many parcels went through the sorting hall that day?

In the morning Kofi arrived at the fun fair with 50 vouchers and was given 20 more at the gate. He exchanged every voucher for 4 game tokens. In the afternoon the games switched to plastic chips, so he swapped every token for 2 chips, and then won 12 more chips at the hoopla. The fair had 9 rides in all. In the evening he lost 423 chips at the shooting gallery, and at closing time the cashier paid him 7 cents for every chip he handed in. How many cents did Kofi receive?

Lucia's cake shop had 73 orders on its books on Monday. On Tuesday 48 new orders came in, and on Wednesday 51 orders were cancelled. On Thursday 66 more orders arrived, and on Friday another 31. Each cupcake in an order sells for 2 dollars. Every order is for 3 cupcakes, and her rival Marco had fewer orders on his books that week. How many cupcakes does Lucia need to bake for the week's orders?

A parent baked 84 muffins and split them equally among the 6 classes at Oakfield School. In Ms. Ortiz's class, the children ate 12 of their muffins at snack time. Later the class received 20 more muffins from the office, and then gave 12 muffins to Mr. Bell's class next door, which had fewer muffins than Ms. Ortiz's class. The muffins Ms. Ortiz's class still had were shared equally among the 5 tables in her room, and the children at each table cut every one of their muffins into 5 pieces. How many pieces of muffin were on the first table?

In the morning a flower seller had 30 bunches of lilies, and 18 wilted bunches had to be thrown out. In the afternoon a delivery brought 48 fresh bunches. Each bunch held 5 stems, so she untied them all and displayed the stems singly, adding 61 loose stems left over from another order. In the evening she sold every stem on the display at 8 dollars each. How many dollars did she take in that evening?

In the morning Aiden set off with 105 flyers for the school play and handed out 79 of them outside the station. In the afternoon he handed out 24 more at the shopping centre, and 1 flyer blew away in the wind. In the evening the drama teacher gave him a fresh bundle of 42 flyers for the next day. His friend Zoe handed out fewer flyers than Aiden that day. How many flyers did Aiden have at the end of the evening?

Farida had 69 stickers and used 60 of them to decorate a poster. She shared the stickers she had left equally among herself, Rana, and Tariq, so each of the 3 friends got the same number. Half an hour later Farida opened a new pack and added 51 stickers to her share. She then traded 41 stickers to Tariq for a comic and received 22 stickers from her teacher. Rana finished the day with fewer stickers than Farida. How many stickers does Farida have now?

The community fridge on Elm Street held 89 packed meals on Monday morning. During the day 42 meals were taken by neighbours, and a dozen volunteers removed 10 meals that had passed their date. On Tuesday a restaurant donated 48 meals to the fridge. On Wednesday 74 meals were taken, and 3 were dropped and had to be thrown out. How many meals are in the fridge now?

In the morning a parking garage held 186 cars. By ten o'clock 58 cars had driven out and 5 had driven in. In the afternoon another 80 cars left. In the evening 61 cars arrived for the theatre show next door, which ran for one hundred and twenty minutes, that is, two hours. How many cars were in the garage at the end of the evening?

A courier named Ali drives 101 kilometres a day, 7 days a week, and kept that up for 4 weeks. On top of that he made a 21-kilometre detour to a depot and a 70-kilometre trip for a special delivery. His van holds 60 litres of fuel. When he handed in his logbook, 1324 kilometres were struck off as personal driving that the company does not pay for. His colleague Ben was paid for fewer kilometres than Ali that month. How many kilometres was Ali paid for?

Nate is tiling a floor and has 30 boxes of mosaic tiles; each box contains 8 packs, and each pack holds 4 tiles. He also has 26 loose tiles from an earlier job in the same pile. For the border pattern he cuts every tile in the pile into 3 equal strips. He then lays 1440 strips along the border. His colleague Rosa has fewer strips left than Nate. How many strips does Nate have left?

In the morning 205 runners lined up for the city half-marathon, and 19 latecomers joined them just before the start, followed by 31 more who had queued at the wrong gate. Every runner took 4 cups of water from the dozen water stations along the course. The winner finished in one hundred and twenty minutes, that is, two hours. In the afternoon the volunteers drank 65 cups themselves while packing up, and in the evening the cleanup crew used 29 more cups. How many cups were used in total that day?

In the morning Jamal sold 50 tickets an hour for 4 hours for the school play. Before lunch 25 tickets were refunded, and 4 tickets were lost in the office and voided. In the afternoon the treasurer counted the sale as 3 dollars for every valid ticket. The play ran for ninety minutes, an hour and a half. In the evening Jamal paid 494 dollars of costume costs out of the ticket money. His co-organiser Kim raised fewer dollars than Jamal. How many dollars did Jamal have left after paying the costs?

A candle maker had 106 boxes with 6 candles in each. She sold 299 candles at a fair and donated 164 candles to a church, leaving the rest on half a shelf in her workshop. Each of her candles burns for 7 hours, and every hour of burning uses 9 grams of wax. How many grams of wax will the candles she has left use up if they all burn out completely?

In the morning Lin picked 17 baskets of apples from the orchard, with 7 apples in every basket. Her friend Mo, who picked fewer apples than Lin, gave her 19 apples from his own basket. In the afternoon Lin sold 127 apples at the roadside stall. In the evening she cut every apple she had left into 7 slices for a pie. How many apple slices did Lin have for the pie?

In the morning a bakery had 129 bread rolls on its shelves and took 37 more out of the oven. By the afternoon a big bake had tripled the number of rolls on the shelves, and a neighbour returned 14 rolls she had bought by mistake, which went back on the shelves. In the evening every roll on the shelves was sold to a canteen at 5 cents each. The bakery then paid 2139 cents for the flour it had used. How many cents did the bakery have left from the sale?
